podcast.title: Plagiarism Allegations Against Trent Reznor (1997)
podcast.body: Mark Anofrio, an LA musician recording under the name Elephant Man, accused Trent Reznor of stealing six of his songs. He claimed to have met Reznor during an internet chat session and subsequently mailed a tape of his compositions to Reznor's home. "On August 18th, 1997, he was notified that an LA musician named Mark Anofrio had accused Trent of stealing six of his songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Case Dismissal (1998)
podcast.body: After initial delays and Anofrio dropping claims on three of the six songs, the case was ultimately brought before a federal judge on December 1, 1998, and subsequently dismissed. "Everything finally ended up before a federal judge on December 1, 1998, at which point the case was thrown out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Copyright Infringement and Unfair Competition Charges
podcast.body: Anofrio charged Trent Reznor with copyright infringement and unfair competition in his plagiarism lawsuit. "He charged Trent with copyright infringement and unfair competition."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Specific Song Allegations
podcast.body: Anofrio alleged that five songs from Nine Inch Nails' 1994 album "The Downward Spiral" ("Closer," "Hurt," "March of the Pigs," "Mr. Self-destruct," and "Downward Spiral") and the song "Burn" (contributed to the "Natural Born Killers" soundtrack) were ripoffs of his "Elephant Man" compositions. "He says, closer, hurt, march of the pigs, Mr. Self-destruct, and downward spiral are all ripoffs of Elephant Man."

xref.title: Plagiarism Lawsuit by Mark Anofrio (1997-1998)
xref.body: On August 18, 1997, Trent Reznor was sued by LA musician Mark Anofrio, who alleged that six of his songs, recorded under the name Elephant Man, were stolen. Anofrio claimed he sent a tape to Reznor after an internet chat session. Five songs from "The Downward Spiral" (1994) and "Burn" from the "Natural Born Killers" soundtrack were identified as alleged ripoffs. The case eventually went before a federal judge on December 1, 1998, and was dismissed. "On August 18th, 1997, he was notified that an LA musician named Mark Anofrio had accused Trent of stealing six of his songs."

xref.title: Plagiarism Suit by Mark Anofrio (1997-1998)
xref.body: Trent Reznor was accused by LA musician Mark Anofrio on August 18, 1997, of stealing six songs, including five from "The Downward Spiral" (1994) and "Burn." Anofrio claimed he had sent recorded material, under the name Elephant Man, to Reznor's home. The case, after delays and Anofrio dropping claims on some songs, was eventually dismissed by a federal judge on December 1, 1998. "On August 18th, 1997, he was notified that an LA musician named Mark Anofrio had accused Trent of stealing six of his songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
